Scope: 3 files, +6 −1, from merge-base `3d7f3ea2` to `dd402c04`. All three are Markdown docs under `docs/agents/`. `c66f89e2` isn't an ancestor of HEAD, so the three-dot diff starts at the merge-base.

## Fix before opening

**F1 · P2 · conventions · CONFIRMED (the agent could not disprove it)**
`docs/agents/module-structure.md:133`
- **What's wrong:** The rule says a module can skip its own `app.module.ts` entry "when the new module only serves that one" module. Two of the four examples it cites serve more than one module:
  - `SiweModule` is imported by `src/modules/auth/auth.module.ts:10` and `src/modules/users/users.module.ts:26`, and both of those are registered separately in `src/app.module.ts:94,118`.
  - `QueuesApiModule` is imported by `src/modules/health/health.module.ts:10`, and also reaches `hooks.module.ts` through `QueuesRepositoryModule` (`src/modules/queues/domain/queues-repository.interface.ts:24`).
  - `backbone` (only `chains`) and `EntitlementsModule` (only `BillingModule`) do fit the rule.
- **Why it matters:** A reviewer or agent checking a new module that serves two consumers gets opposite answers from the condition and from the examples.
- **Fix:** Either change the condition to "imported by the registered module(s) it serves, with no HTTP surface of its own", or drop `siwe` and `queues` from the examples.

**F2 · P2 · conventions · WEAKENED (likelihood lowered from L3 to L2; impact stays I3)**
`docs/agents/api-dtos-and-validation.md:113`
- **What's wrong:** It gives "a field the upstream never actually populated" as an example of a field no client could have parsed. That doesn't follow. If the field was declared nullable (`.nullish()`, sent as `"x": null`), every released client has been receiving and decoding that key. Strict decoders, such as kotlinx.serialization or generated OpenAPI clients, fail when the key disappears.
- **Evidence:** The repo's own `docs/agents/remarks.md:192` says a missing key and a `null` value are different wire payloads. The precedent behind this rule, `validUntil` (`z.number().nullish()`), is exactly this ambiguous case.
- **Why only weakened:** The rule already requires a justification in the PR description, so both the author and the reviewer would have to miss the problem.
- **Fix:** Narrow the example to "a field that was never present in the response (omitted, not `null`)".
